sections.html:
Kokomo is the Howard County seat, about 60 miles north of Indianapolis. The 2020 count was 59,604 residents. The median owner-occupied home value is $137,400, and 63.0% of housing units are owner-occupied, with a median gross rent of $939. At that price level, repair costs can be a large share of what a house is worth, which is one reason repair-heavy sales are common here.

Automobile manufacturing is still a big share of local jobs, with Stellantis transmission, casting and engine plants and the StarPlus Energy joint venture. When a plant adds shifts or cuts them, housing demand can follow, and sellers tied to a job change often need a firm closing date.

A normal Kokomo year brings 44.40 inches of precipitation and 34.1 inches of snow. Temperatures have ranged from 110 degrees down to minus 26, so heating and cooling systems and roofs see real use.

Questions buyers raise most often:

  • How old is the roof, and has storm damage ever been fixed?
  • Does the basement stay dry, and does the sump pump work?
  • Is the lot close to Wildcat Creek or in a mapped flood zone?
  • How old are the furnace and the air conditioner?

Kokomo's municipal code, Chapter 152, sets minimum standards for dwellings. It covers owner and occupant duties, entry for inspections, notices of violation, Review Board hearings and enforcement orders. Maintenance items include foundations and framing, stairs and porches, gutters and downspouts, plumbing fixtures, water heaters, heating and electrical outlets.

An unfit dwelling can be condemned and placarded, and a condemned building must be vacated. A Rental Housing Officer may inspect structures at reasonable times, with an inspection warrant available if the owner refuses. Chapter 159 covers rental housing, so check current requirements with the city before selling a rental.

An open violation or placard can slow a conventional sale. Phone the city and ask what is outstanding on your property.

At a median value of $137,400, even a mid-size repair bill can cut deeply into a Kokomo owner's proceeds. Go through the house as a buyer's inspector would and list what you find: roof, furnace, water heater, foundation, basement moisture, storm damage. Get rough quotes. Then ask what the house would fetch after the work, how many weeks it takes and whether you can pay up front.

A buyer with a mortgage usually responds to the inspection with a repair request or a lower offer. A cash buyer prices condition from the start. When repairs would swallow most of the gain, selling as-is can net a similar amount with far less effort.

sections.h2: Recording a deed in Howard County
sections.html:
Howard County Recorder, in the Administration Center at 220 North Main Street, Room 330, files Kokomo deeds. Walk-in hours run Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., and the phone is 765-456-2210.

This office holds the permanent public record of who owned what, including deeds, mortgages and liens, and its files reach back to 1844. Most copies cost $1 per page.

Before the deed is filed, Indiana wants a sales disclosure form: the county assessor reviews it and the auditor files it. A title company ordinarily takes care of this for you.

sections.h2: Property tax and the homestead deduction
sections.html: Howard County bills property tax twice a year, with installments due May 10 and November 10. At closing the title company prorates whichever one lands near your sale date and pays any tax owed from your proceeds. Owners who live in the house may have the homestead deduction, the lesser of $45,000 or 60% of gross assessed value. The county auditor can explain how it shows up on your bill.

The Kokomo-Center Township Consolidated School Corporation serves most neighborhoods inside city limits. Check a specific address against the district's boundaries before you describe it to a buyer.

U.S. 31 bypasses Kokomo on the east, and the old route is State Road 931. The Kokomo City-Line Trolley runs five bus routes, and Miller Transportation offers intercity service to Indianapolis and South Bend.

Several situations come up again and again among Kokomo owners who contact us.

  • Older houses where roof, furnace or foundation work was put off.
  • Storm damage never fully repaired.
  • Tenants in place, or a rental with code questions.
  • Inherited homes with several heirs.
  • Job changes linked to the area's plants.

Before you talk to buyers, write down the age of the roof, furnace and water heater, any storm or water history, and whether anyone lives in it. A clear list lets a buyer price repairs honestly.

If a storm hit the house, gather photos, contractor estimates and insurance paperwork. For a rental, gather the lease and rent ledger. For an inherited house, ask the title company or an attorney which documents the recorder will need before a deed can be prepared.

sections.h2: Steps from first call to closing
sections.html:
1. Send us the address and describe the house, any tenants and any open city notices.
  2. We look at the property and make an offer.
  3. If you accept, the title company opens the file and searches the deed for liens and unpaid taxes.
  4. You sign the deed paperwork and the sales disclosure form.
  5. The deed is recorded in Room 330 and you receive your proceeds.

Delays usually come from the title search: an old lien, a deed that still shows a former owner or probate papers still outstanding. Mention anything like that on the first call.

sections.h2: How a cash sale works here
sections.html:
We buy Kokomo houses as-is, so storm damage, deferred repairs and code issues need not be fixed first. Tell us about the house and we make an offer. Once you accept, a title company searches the deed and sets a closing date. You skip staging, repairs and showings.

Compare offers in writing and ask every buyer who pays for title and recording. Get the closing date in writing too.

A Kokomo rental sold with a tenant keeps its lease, so gather the lease and rent ledger and tell any buyer the terms. Confirm with the city whether anything is outstanding under the rental housing rules before closing.

An inherited house may need probate before a deed can be prepared, and it may need a clean-out. Heirs who live elsewhere often pay utilities, insurance and tax on a house nobody uses. Collect the estate papers, tax bill and keys, and ask the title company what the deed needs before closing day.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed in Kokomo?
faqs.a: At the Howard County Recorder's Office, 220 North Main Street, Room 330, Kokomo. The phone number is 765-456-2210.

Kokomo's code includes a Rental Housing Officer who can inspect structures at reasonable times, with an inspection warrant if the owner does not consent.

faqs.q: When are Howard County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Two installments a year, on May 10 and November 10. Your closing agent usually prorates the installment.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Kokomo house with code violations?
faqs.a: Yes, but open violations or a condemnation placard can slow a conventional sale. Ask the city what is outstanding, and compare written cash offers.
